name: Chautauqua Park
unique: The Flatirons rise straight out of a 1898 Chautauqua campus, with a dining hall, a ranger cottage and trails that climb into the rock in 20 minutes.
buzz: The First and Second Flatiron trails are the local workout and the lawn is a picnic spot; parking fills by nine on weekends and the shuttle runs in summer.

name: Celestial Seasonings Tea Tour
unique: A walk through the tea factory past the mint room, where the smell is so strong visitors are warned, ending in a tasting room of every blend.
buzz: The mint room is the story everyone tells and the tasting is generous; the tour is free and requires a reservation.

name: Fiske Planetarium
unique: One of the largest planetariums in the country, with a dome 60 feet across and student led shows that include live tours of the current sky.
buzz: The live star talks are better than the recorded shows and the laser nights are the student tradition; check the schedule before driving.

name: Denver Art Museum
unique: Daniel Libeskind's angular steel building and a collection of Native American, Latin American and western art, including the finest collection of Indigenous art in the country.
buzz: The Indigenous arts galleries are the reason curators visit and the architecture is the family puzzle; the building is confusing and the map helps.

name: Denver Botanic Gardens
unique: Twenty four acres with a Japanese garden, a tropical conservatory and a Rocky Mountain alpine collection that grows plants from above treeline.
buzz: The Japanese garden and the conservatory are the winter stops; the summer concert series on the lawn is the local date night.

name: Molly Brown House Museum
unique: The 1889 Capitol Hill house of the Titanic survivor and suffragist, restored with period rooms and a tour that separates the myth from the life.
buzz: The guides are good at cutting through the Unsinkable Molly Brown legend; the house is small and the tour runs on the hour.

name: Breckenridge Ski Resort
unique: Five peaks above a preserved gold rush main street, with above treeline bowls, a high speed gondola and a town you can walk at the base.
buzz: The high alpine terrain is the draw and the altitude is real; the town is lively and the lift lines on peak weekends are the complaint.

name: Country Boy Mine
customer: Families, history kids, gold rush fans
unique: A real gold mine tunnel you walk into with a hard hat, and a hillside of ore chutes and buildings above Breckenridge, with gold panning at the end.
buzz: The underground tour is short and cool and the panning keeps children busy; it is the best rainy day activity in town.

name: Iowa Hill Trail
unique: A short trail through the remains of a hydraulic gold mining operation, with sluice cuts, a miner's cabin and a view over the town.
buzz: Locals use it as an easy evening walk and the signs explain what the ditches were for; it is free and takes an hour.

name: Vail Mountain
unique: The back bowls that changed American skiing, 5,300 acres across seven miles, with a village at the base built to look like a Tyrolean town.
buzz: Skiers come for the back bowls and the powder days; the front side gets tracked out fast and the village is expensive.

name: Betty Ford Alpine Gardens
unique: The highest botanical garden in the country at 8,200 feet, with rock gardens of alpine plants from around the world and a waterfall below the ski slopes.
buzz: Gardeners call it a miracle of microclimate and it is free; the peak is late June and the paths are steep.

name: Beaver Creek
unique: A resort built around a pedestrian village and a bird sanctuary, with groomed cruisers, a downhill race course and cookie time at the base each afternoon.
buzz: Families like the easy layout and the ski school; experts find it tame compared with Vail and the village is quiet at night.

name: Maroon Bells
unique: Two maroon striped peaks reflected in a glacial lake at the end of the most photographed road in Colorado, with trails into the Elk Mountains.
buzz: The lake at dawn is the photograph and the shuttle is mandatory in summer; the parking reservation system catches people out.

name: Aspen Art Museum
unique: A free museum in a Shigeru Ban building with a woven wood screen, a rooftop sculpture garden and a glass elevator that opens onto views of Aspen Mountain.
buzz: The roof deck and the building are worth the stop even if the exhibition is between shows; admission is free and it is a one hour visit.

name: Ashcroft Ghost Town
unique: A silver boom town of 2,000 people reduced to a handful of cabins in a meadow at the end of a dirt road, with the hotel and saloon still standing.
buzz: The setting under Castle Peak is the reason to come and the buildings are unrestored; the road is rough and the site is free.

name: Glenwood Hot Springs
unique: The world's largest mineral hot springs pool, a block long and fed by a Yampah spring at 122 degrees, with the Colorado River running past the wall.
buzz: The pool is the family side and the smaller therapy pool is quieter; it is busiest in ski season and the water is body temperature.

name: Hanging Lake
unique: A travertine lake hanging above Glenwood Canyon, with turquoise water, fallen logs and a waterfall, reached by a steep mile of switchbacks.
buzz: The permit system limits the crowd and the trail is steep and rocky; no swimming and the shuttle from Glenwood is the way in.

name: Glenwood Caverns
unique: A cave system inside Iron Mountain reached by a gondola, with formations lit in color and a cliffside coaster and swing on top.
buzz: The cave tour is the reason to come and the rides are the surprise; the combo ticket is the way to do both.

name: Colorado National Monument
unique: Red sandstone canyons and monoliths above the Grand Valley, with a 23 mile rim road, tunnel and trailheads that drop into the canyon.
buzz: The rim rock drive at sunset is the experience and the Monument Canyon trail is the hike; the road is narrow with cyclists.

name: Museum of the West
unique: A regional museum with Ute baskets, a taxidermy hall and a courtyard of pioneer cabins and farm equipment behind the main building.
buzz: The Ute collection is the serious part and the outdoor village is good with children; it is small and the staff are local experts.

name: Powderhorn Mountain
unique: A small ski hill on the Grand Mesa with a view into the Colorado National Monument, lift tickets half the price of the destination resorts and no lift lines.
buzz: Locals call it the best value in the state and the terrain is modest; the drive up the mesa can be snowy and the lodge is basic.

name: Crested Butte
unique: A ski mountain above a preserved Victorian mining town, with extreme terrain and a July wildflower bloom that draws botanists from other countries.
buzz: Skiers come for the steeps and the town is the reason to stay; the wildflower festival in July books a year out.

name: Taylor Reservoir
unique: A high reservoir below the Elk Mountains where the Taylor River runs out and rainbow trout stack up, ringed by forest service campgrounds.
buzz: Fishermen come for the tailwater below the dam and the jeep roads into the mountains are the local adventure; the water is cold and the wind picks up.

name: Curecanti National Recreation Area
unique: Three reservoirs in the Gunnison River gorge, with a 5.5 mile trail to the Morrow Point boat tour and osprey nests on the canyon walls.
buzz: The Morrow Point boat tour through the gorge is the hidden gem and it runs on a schedule; the lakes are windy in the afternoon.

name: Zapata Falls
unique: A short climb to a slot where the Zapata Creek drops into a cave behind the rock, with the Great Sand Dunes spread out below the trail.
buzz: The last stretch is a wade through cold water and the payoff is a waterfall inside a cave; the road is rough for low cars.

name: Colorado Gators Reptile Park
unique: A tilapia farm that became an alligator rescue in the San Luis Valley, with 200 gators in geothermal water and a chance to hold a small one.
buzz: People cannot believe alligators live in Colorado; the staff are rescuing animals and the feeding shows are the reason to check times.

name: Royal Gorge Bridge
unique: The highest suspension bridge in the country over the Arkansas River, with a gondola, a zip line and a skycoaster above a 1,000 foot gorge.
buzz: The bridge walk is the free thrill and the add ons cost extra; the park was rebuilt after a 2013 fire and the views are the point.

name: Skyline Drive
unique: A one way road along the crest of a dinosaur fossil ridge, with drops on both sides and a view of the Arkansas valley and the Sangre de Cristo range.
buzz: Locals take visitors up at sunset and the road is narrow and one way; dinosaur tracks were found along the ridge.

name: Mollie Kathleen Gold Mine
unique: A original gold mine cage drops you 1,000 feet underground into tunnels where ore cars, drills and stopes are still in place, guided by miners.
buzz: The cage ride is the thrill and the guides are retired miners; it is cold underground and the tour is the only way in.

name: Cripple Creek Heritage Center
unique: A free museum above the gold camp explaining the 1890s rush, the labor war and the open pit mine that swallowed part of the town.
buzz: The view from the deck and the film are the quick history lesson; it pairs with the Mollie Kathleen mine down the road.
